title: Annotatio IV §.XIII close: Erigena coeval truth; Amalarius / Rabanus / Walafrid — stop before §.XIV
pass_a_gloss: Still more expressly, that John Scotus Erigena enunciated and comprehended in writing all the Eucharistic truth handed down by Bertram, his Coeval and Fellow-soldier, summoned together by Charles the Bald — although his Treatise by injury of the times is lost, or rather by the perverse zeal of the Roman Pontiff and other malevolents was handed to Vulcan — other Writings of this Man make faith, On the Division of nature, vindicated from destruction by the Oxford men in the year 81 of the prior age… See the testimonies of other Orthodox Writers of the Ninth Age concerning the Eucharist — Amalarius, Rabanus Maurus, Walafrid Strabo, and Bertram himself — vindicated against the Pontificals in Durham from p. 88 to p. 97.
pass_b_english: Erigena, Bertram’s coeval fellow summoned by Charles the Bald, stated the same Eucharistic truth — his treatise lost (or burned by hostile zeal), but On the Division of Nature (Oxford recovery) and other writings make faith.
See also Amalarius, Rabanus Maurus, Walafrid Strabo, and Bertram himself vindicated in Durham pp. 88–97. Stop before §.XIV (tenth century).
source_text: Adhuc disertius Johannem Scotum Erigenam, omnem Bertrami, Coævi sui & Comilitionis, à Carolo Calvo unà evocati, de Eucharistia traditam veritatem enunciasse scriptoque comprehendisse, etsi ejus Tractatus injuria temporum deperditus, vel potiùs Pontificis Romani & aliorum malevolorum perverso zelô, traditus Vulcano sit, fidem faciunt alia Viri hujus Scripta, de Divisione naturæ, per Oxonienses, Anno superioris seculi 81. ab interitu vindicata… Aliorum Seculi Noni Scriptorum de Eucharistia Orthodoxorum testimonia, Amalarii puta, Rabani Mauri, Walafridi Strabonis, ut & ipsius Bertrami, contra Pontificios vindicata vide apud Dunelmensem à p. 88. ad p. 97.
